Chapter 5 • Fields

5.3 Tensor Fields and notation

  • A (smooth) \( (r,s) \)-tensor field is a \( C^\infty(\mathcal{M}) \)-multilinear map \[ T : \underbrace{\Gamma T^* \mathcal{M} \times \dots \times \Gamma T^* \mathcal{M}}_{r\text{-terms}} \times \underbrace{\Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \dots \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M}}_{s\text{-terms}} \overset{\scriptstyle \begin{array}{c} \sim \\[-10pt] ... \\[-6pt] \sim \end{array}}{\longrightarrow} C^\infty(\mathcal{M}). \] In particular, a \((0,1)\)-tensor field is a covector field, i.e. an element of \(\Gamma T^* \mathcal{M}\), and a \((1,0)\)-tensor field is a vector field, i.e. an element of \(\Gamma T \mathcal{M}\) (since the dual of \(\Gamma T^* \mathcal{M}\) is \(\Gamma T \mathcal{M}\)).

  • So far, given a chart \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\) around \(p\), we have expanded vectors and covectors at that point in the chart-induced bases of \(T_p\mathcal{M}\) and \(T^*_p\mathcal{M}\) which, in the compact notation of Subsections 4.1.2 and 4.2.2, read \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} v_{\gamma, p} = x^i_p \, (\partial x_i)_p \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad ; \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} (df)_p = \mathtt{x}_i^p \, (dx^i)_p, \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \] with \(x^i_p = \dot{\gamma}^i_{\mathcal{U}}(\lambda_0)\), \((\partial x_i)_p = \left( \partial / \partial \mathscr{X}^i \right)_p\), \(\mathtt{x}_i^p = (df)_p\big((\partial x_i)_p\big)\) and \((dx^i)_p = (d\mathscr{X}^i)_p\), and where the Einstein summation convention is implied. Both the components and the basis elements refer to the single point \(p\).

  • At the level of fields, each of these expressions splits into two parts, both of which are promoted from the single point \(p\) to the whole chart domain \(\mathcal{U}\):

    1. Basis fields. Dropping the point \(p\), as done in Section 5.1, the basis elements become smooth sections over \(\mathcal{U}\), the chart-induced basis vector and covector fields: \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} : \mathcal{U} &\longrightarrow T\mathcal{U} \\ p &\longmapsto \left( \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \right)_p \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad ; \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} d\mathscr{X}^i : \mathcal{U} &\longrightarrow T^*\mathcal{U} \\ p &\longmapsto (d\mathscr{X}^i)_p. \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \] On the overlap \(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\) with a second chart \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\), they transform as \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} = \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \, \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad ; \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} d\mathscr{X}^i = \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \, d\mathscr{Y}^j, \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \] where the entries of the Jacobian are now functions rather than numbers: \begin{align*} \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} : \mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V} &\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\ p &\longmapsto \left( \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \right)_p = \partial_j \left[ \mathscr{X}^i \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} \right] \big( \mathscr{Y}(p) \big), \end{align*} i.e. \(\left( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \right)^i_{j} \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V})\), and correspondingly for \(\partial \mathscr{Y}^j / \partial \mathscr{X}^i = \left( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}} \right)^j_{i}\).

    2. Component functions. The components, real numbers at \(p\), become smooth functions on \(\mathcal{U}\), obtained by letting each field act on the basis of the other kind: \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} x^i \coloneqq \left. \mathcal{X} \right|_\mathcal{U} \left\lfloor \mathscr{X}^i \right\rceil \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U}) \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad ; \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \mathtt{x}_i \coloneqq \left. df \right|_\mathcal{U} \left\lceil \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \right\rfloor \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U}), \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \] so that, at each point \(p\) with \(\mathcal{X}(p) = v_{\gamma, p}\), they return the components above, \(x^i(p) = x^i_p\) and \(\mathtt{x}_i(p) = \mathtt{x}_i^p\). Denoting by \(y^j\) and \(\mathtt{y}_j\) the component functions w.r.t. \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\), they transform on \(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\) as \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} x^i = \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \, y^j \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad ; \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \mathtt{x}_i = \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \, \mathtt{y}_j. \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \]

  • Putting both parts together, vector and covector fields are expanded over \(\mathcal{U}\) as \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \left. \mathcal{X} \right|_\mathcal{U} = \underbrace{x^i}_{\in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})} \odot_\Gamma \underbrace{\frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}}_{\in \Gamma T\mathcal{U}} \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad ; \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \left. df \right|_\mathcal{U} = \underbrace{\mathtt{x}_i}_{\in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})} \odot^*_\Gamma \underbrace{d\mathscr{X}^i}_{\in \Gamma T^*\mathcal{U}}, \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \] and, extending the compact notation to fields by dropping the point \(p\) from the basis elements and the s-multiplication symbols, \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \left. \mathcal{X} \right|_\mathcal{U} = x^i \, \partial x_i \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad ; \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \left. df \right|_\mathcal{U} = \mathtt{x}_i \, dx^i. \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \] In the same way, an \((r,s)\)-tensor field is expanded over \(\mathcal{U}\) as \begin{align*} \left. T \right|_\mathcal{U} &= T^{i_1 \dots i_r}_{j_1 \dots j_s} \; \partial x_{i_1} \otimes \dots \otimes \partial x_{i_r} \otimes dx^{j_1} \otimes \dots \otimes dx^{j_s}, \\ T^{i_1 \dots i_r}_{j_1 \dots j_s} &\coloneqq T\big( dx^{i_1}, \dots, dx^{i_r}, \partial x_{j_1}, \dots, \partial x_{j_s} \big) \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U}), \end{align*} whose component functions transform with one Jacobian factor per index, as those of \(x^i\) (upper) and \(\mathtt{x}_i\) (lower) above.

  • With this notation the letter “\(x\)” appears in several fonts, and its meaning depends on the context: \(\mathscr{X}^i\) are the coordinate functions of the chart, \(x^i_p\) and \(\mathtt{x}_i^p\) are real numbers at a point \(p\), \(x^i\) and \(\mathtt{x}_i\) are functions on \(\mathcal{U}\), and \((\partial x_i)_p\), \((dx^i)_p\) are basis elements at the point \(p\), while \(\partial x_i\), \(dx^i\) are the corresponding basis fields over \(\mathcal{U}\). Care must be taken to avoid misinterpretation.
